approach: Fix where the timeout becomes a failed verdict, with no file outside the brief's deliverables. (1) verify.rs: change the type of `VerdictInputs.verifier_failure` from `Option<String>` to `Option<VerifierFailure>`, a new enum `{ Incomplete(String), TimedOut(String) }`. Every existing literal says `verifier_failure: None`, so it still compiles and send_back.rs needs no edit. `judge` gives `TimedOut` the reason `unjudged: the verifier timed out (...); the criteria were not judged`, separate from 'the verifier did not complete'. It writes 'unjudged' criterion evidence, skips 'returned no verdict', invents no finding, and never passes. The verdict stays `Fail` (athena-data is untouched). (2) run/verification.rs: a verifier invocation that ended `InvocationOutcome::TimedOut` sets a new local `verifier_timeout`, not `verifier_failure`. On a first timeout the same loop reruns the verifier once on the same locked snapshot, the same `check_runs` and the same `inputs`, so no check runs again; the cap of two runs is shared with the snapshot-change rerun. A timeout still present after the loop is passed to `judge` and closes the job as `Failed` with a reason that starts with the existing `disk::ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX`. `StopCause::of` already reads that as `OtherEnvironment`, so `is_environment_reason`, `resumable_stop` and `settle_resume_marks` already treat it as a resumable stop that is not a rejection. disk.rs needs no change. The reason is built by `self.failure(ctx, &reason)`, the call a check timeout uses at run/mod.rs:1569. The Verification record is still written, with the unjudged reason. (3) Tests drive the real `go` flow with a scripted verifier turn, plus `judge` unit tests. (4) Docs, CHANGELOG, and the display `next` line.

decisions.choice: Make `verifier_failure` a typed `Option<VerifierFailure>` with variants `Incomplete(String)` and `TimedOut(String)`, instead of adding a second field.
decisions.reason: The root cause is that one untyped string carried both a timeout and a real failure, and both produced 'the verifier did not complete' and a failed verdict. A typed value keeps the two apart where `judge` reads them, and the pass rule (`verifier_failure.is_none()`) already covers both, so a timeout can never pass. Every existing literal is `verifier_failure: None`, so it compiles unchanged. That removes the edit to run/send_back.rs, which is not a deliverable (findings 3).

rejected.why: Every literal must then name the field, which forces an edit to run/send_back.rs, a file outside the deliverables.

rejected.option: Match 'deadline' or 'timed out' in the free text of `verifier_failure`
rejected.why: A word list over free text. The invocation already carries a typed `InvocationOutcome::TimedOut`.
It changes record schemas, the gate's reading and the round-trip tests. The brief puts the gate's reading out of scope and lists no athena-data file.

decisions.choice: Close an unresolved timeout as `OutcomeState::Failed` with a reason starting `disk::ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` ('environment: unjudged: the verifier timed out ...; this is the verifier's time, not the work, `athena retry <job>`'), built in verification.rs with `self.failure`. `verification_passed` is None and nothing is `verified`.
decisions.reason: A prefixed reason is already read as an environment stop by `StopCause::of` (`OtherEnvironment`), so `athena retry` can resume it and `settle_resume_marks` keeps the resume mark. This is the same path a check timeout takes, and it needs no new `StopCause` variant, so disk.rs stays untouched (finding 4). The job is not Rejected, so the work is not recorded as rejected. The resume mark is already written once the checks pass (run/mod.rs ~1577), so a retry resumes at the verifier with the recorded checks.

rejected.why: The existing prefix handling gives the same behavior. disk.rs is not on the brief's list.

rejected.option: Keep `Rejected` and change only the reason text
rejected.why: The job would still count as a rejection of the work, and a retry could not resume at the verifier.
That state means the producer timed out, and `timeout_seed` resumes from kept producer work.

decisions.choice: Rerun once inside the existing verifier loop, sharing its two-run cap, on the same snapshot and inputs.
decisions.reason: The loop already reruns once for a snapshot change. The checks and brief are already built, so the retry reuses the gathered check results, as the introspections propose. The snapshot-equality check runs first, so a timed-out run that altered the snapshot takes the existing fresh-snapshot path.

rejected.option: Per-criterion incremental saving, or a deadline that scales with the work
rejected.why: Out of scope. `verifier_timeout_s` in athena.toml must not change.

verify.rs: add `VerifierFailure` and `pub const UNJUDGED_PREFIX: &str = "unjudged"`. Change the field type and its doc comment, which names the root cause. In `judge`: `Incomplete` keeps the current 'the verifier did not complete: ...' reason; `TimedOut` pushes `unjudged: the verifier timed out ({detail}); the criteria were not judged`, does not add 'returned no verdict', and gives a criterion with no result the evidence 'unjudged: the verifier timed out' and no invented finding. The two `is_none()` checks at ~499 and ~528 stay, so a timeout never passes. The `verifier_failure: None` literals compile unchanged.

verification.rs: add `let mut verifier_timeout: Option<String> = None;`. In the `Ok((voutput, vrecord))` arm, when `voutput.outcome == InvocationOutcome::TimedOut`, set `verifier_timeout` to the record detail (default 'deadline reached') and leave `verifier_failure` unset. Other non-success outcomes keep the current code. Do not add 'no valid verdict' for a timeout. After the snapshot-equality check passes, if `verifier_timeout.is_some() && verifier_runs < 2`, print a ui line, clear `verifier_timeout`, `verdict_output`, `commands_run` and `verifier_invocation`, and `continue` (still recording the timed-out invocation in `closing.new_invocations`). The snapshot-change branch also clears `verifier_timeout`. The budget `break` and the snapshot-lock break leave a set timeout in place.

verification.rs, at the `judge` call: pass `verifier_failure: verifier_timeout.clone().map(VerifierFailure::TimedOut).or(verifier_failure.clone().map(VerifierFailure::Incomplete))`. After the Verification is built, if `verifier_timeout` is still Some: keep `changed_paths`, set `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, &reason)` with `reason = format!("{ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX} unjudged: the verifier timed out ({detail}); the criteria were not judged, this is the verifier's time and not the work. `athena retry {id}`")`, set `verification_passed = None`, `verified = None`, and keep `closing.verification = Some(..)`. Otherwise keep the Landed/Rejected mapping. Check run/close.rs 46-55 uses `happened.reason` first.

verify.rs tests: (a) a timeout with no output gives Fail, a reason starting `unjudged`, no 'did not complete', no 'returned no verdict', no Major or Blocker finding, and unjudged evidence. (b) A timeout beside a pass output is still Fail. (c) `Incomplete` still gives Fail with 'did not complete'. (d) A blocking failed check gives 'check test failed' and Fail. (e) A judged fail gives "the verifier's verdict is fail". (f) A pre-existing failing check with a pass verdict still passes.

Test 2 times out on every run, asserts exactly 2 runs, Failed (not Rejected), reason starts 'environment:' and contains 'unjudged', Verification Fail with a reason starting `UNJUDGED_PREFIX` and none containing 'did not complete', `is_environment_reason`, `resumable_stop`. risks.risk: The Verification record has final_verdict Fail while the outcome is Failed, not Rejected. A gate invariant or consumer may assume Fail goes with Rejected. A grep of athena-gate/src for verification and Failed found nothing.
risks.mitigation: The end-to-end test goes through the real `go` flow and the records writer. Run the whole `cargo test --locked`, including the athena-gate and athena-cli lifecycle tests. If something asserts the pairing, keep the state Failed and loosen only that assertion.

risks.risk: Changing the field type breaks a caller I did not find. The grep shows only `verifier_failure: None` literals (verify.rs tests, send_back.rs:270) and the three reads in `judge`.
risks.mitigation: The compiler lists any other. None-literals compile unchanged, so send_back.rs and disk.rs stay untouched.

risks.risk: The retry runs a verifier that may time out again and spends budget.
risks.mitigation: The cap is two runs. `check_budget` runs at the top of each pass. If it refuses the rerun, the first timeout stays set and the job ends as unjudged, not 'did not complete'; the producer tests this only if the loop makes it cheap.

risks.risk: `go_with_stages` still introspects a Failed job, so an unjudged stop can start an introspection about the work.
risks.mitigation: Left unchanged: check-timeout stops behave the same today. Stated in the open questions.

risks.risk: The dropped candidate jobs (run.rs trailer, spec.toml and so on) get mixed in.
risks.mitigation: Only the files in `files` are touched. athena.toml, defaults.toml and workflows are unchanged.

demonstrations.method: Two end-to-end tests in run_pin_tests.rs call `run_with(&config(true), ..)`, which reaches `Athena::go`, `verification_stage` and `judge`. The `Tweak` closure (the `Arc<dyn Fn(&AgentInvocation, &mut FakeTurn)>` passed to `athena_with`) acts on the Verifier role only. It records the run in a shared counter and sets `turn.outcome = InvocationOutcome::TimedOut`, `turn.structured = None` and `turn.detail = Some("deadline of 2400s reached")` on run 0 only (test 1) or on every run (test 2). Guards: checks pass first, so the study job reaches the verifier. The deadline is a scripted outcome, so no real time passes; the retry, the classification and the closing live in production code.

Test 2 (timeout twice): exactly 2 runs, not 3; state `Failed`, not `Rejected`; closing reason starts 'environment:' and contains 'unjudged'; `verification.final_verdict == Fail` with a reason starting `UNJUDGED_PREFIX` and none containing 'did not complete'; `is_environment_reason(&finished.reason)`; `resumable_stop(Closed(Failed), Some(&reason))` holds.

open_questions: Should an unjudged Failed job skip the introspection that `go_with_stages` starts for Rejected and Failed? The plan leaves it unchanged, as a check timeout does today.
Does any gate or status consumer require a Fail verification to sit with a Rejected outcome? A grep of athena-gate/src found no such rule, but invariant.rs and the status code were not read in full.
When the first run times out and `check_budget` refuses the rerun, should the reason be unjudged or the budget text? The plan picks unjudged because the timeout stays set.
